title: Electoral Commission of Zambia v Belemu Sibanze [2024] ZMCC 22 (14 October 2024)
case_name: Electoral Commission of Zambia v Belemu Sibanze
issue_tags: Article 52(4) — nomination challenge (7 days to file, 21 days to hear)
Article 1(1) and 1(3) — supremacy of the Constitution
Bernard Kanengo v Attorney General — followed
Originating Summons under Order IV rule 2(2) CCR
jurisdiction of High Court in nomination challenges
outcome_detail: Originating Summons (Order IV rule 2(2) Constitutional Court Rules) by the Electoral Commission of Zambia for interpretation of the constitutional timelines governing by-elections. The Court (paragraphs [38]–[45]) interpreted: (i) the 90-day by-election timetable in Article 57 is absolute and runs continuously without stopping; (ii) once the Electoral Commission is notified of a vacancy, it is under compulsion to set in motion and conclude the by-election process within 90 days; (iii) the only constitutionally mandated legal challenge that may be mounted during the 90-day process is a nomination challenge under Article 52(4), which must be filed within 7 days of close of nominations and heard within 21 days of lodgment; (iv) once the 21 days expires the High Court is divested of jurisdiction (following Hakainde Hichilema and Bernard Kanengo). Each party bears their own costs. Classified as `other` because this is a pure constitutional interpretation under originating summons — no petition or appeal is disposed of.
